newsitem.title: USA: IDEX sees Q3, Q4 profits rising vs 1996.
newsitem.headline: IDEX sees Q3, Q4 profits rising vs 1996.

text.p: IDEX Corp said Tuesday it expects profits in the next two quarters to top last year's third and fourth quarters and second half results to at least reach those of the first half.
"The pace of incoming orders has been steady, our recent acquisitions are contributing nicely to earnings and the company's prospects remain good," said Donald Boyce, chairman and president.
"We expect earnings in the next two quarters to exceed those of the corresponding 1996 quarters and second half results to at least match, if not exceed, first half results," Boyce added.
IDEX on Tuesday reported second quarter earnings of $0.50 a share versus $0.43 last year and first half earnings of $0.95 a share versus $0.84.

"For the longer term, we remain confident of IDEX's prospects given our strong market positions, new product and international emphasis and use of the company's fine cash flow to cut debt and interest expense or make acquisitions following our disciplined approach," Boyce said.
International sales accounted for 40 percent of the total in the first half of the year, up from 38 percent in the first half of 1996.

IDEX said second quarter operating margins of 17.5 percent were up slightly from first quarter but off by about 0.06 percent versus last year's second quarter. The company said acquired companies had a slight negative effect but have improving margins.
